newsitem.title: GERMANY: Continental's profit jump fuels share rise.
newsitem.headline: Continental's profit jump fuels share rise.

text.p: German tyre-maker Continental AG on Wednesday reported a 62 percent jump in pre-tax profits for the first nine months of the year, sparking a rally in the company's shares on the Frankfurt stock exchange.
Pre-tax earnings to the end of September surged to 125 million marks ($83.26 million) from 77 million the year before, while sales rose 2.6 percent to 7.63 billion marks.
"We expect strong winter tyre sales to enable fourth quarter operating results to reach the very good levels of a year ago," the company said in a letter to shareholders.
Continental attributed the improvement to gains from lower-cost production achieved by moving some of its operations out of Germany and Ireland to Portugal, the Czech Republic and France.

The figures were a little better than analysts had forecast and sparked a rally in the company's share price. Shares jumped 4.5 percent in heavy trade immediately after the announcement, before settling back. Conti shares were at 26.28 marks at the end of bourse floor trade, up 3.9 percent.
Analysts said the company's cost-cutting moves were paying off.

"They took a charge earlier in the year for closing a plant in Ireland, so those costs were not counted against the third quarter results," said Peter Seppelsericki of a Trinkhaus and Burkhart in Dusseldorf.
"I expect profit will continue on this path as they move operations to low-wage countries."
Continental's profit rise came as Europe's weak economy limited sales to 7.63 billion marks, up only 2.6 percent from the first nine months of 1995.

Without breaking out exact profit figures, Continental said its ContiTech and car tyre units posted gains, while the truck tyre business narrowed its losses without breaking even. Its U.S. subsidiary saw sales fall but still turned a profit.

ContiTech, which makes components for passenger cars and plastic products, reported a 5.8 percent rise in revenue to 2.24 billion marks. Sales in the car tyre business rose 2.3 percent to 2.94 billion marks, helped by strong sales of winter tyres.
The truck tyre unit maintained its market share, but sales slumped 7.1 percent to 800 million marks as demand for trucks and heavy equipment remained weak.
Continental General Tire, the US unit, was helped by the strong dollar, as sales fell 2.5 percent drop in sales to 1.53 billion marks. On a dollar basis, sales fell 6.3 percent.

The automotive systems business, which develops complete brake and wheel systems for car manufacturers, started production sites at Volvo and Mercedes-Benz plants in the third quarter, Continental said.

To cut costs in the third quarter, Continental shut its Dublin plant and moved another from Traiskirchen, Austria, to Barum in the Czech Republic. It also transfered some work from its Hanover-Stoecken plant to others in Lousado, Portugal, and Sarreguemines in France.
The company, which was replaced by Munich Re on Germany's DAX index of 30 blue-chip stocks in September, had 46,382 employees on September 30, 4.1 percent below the year-earlier level.

In the first half, pretax profits doubled to 120 million marks as a result of the company's restructuring measures. In its third quarter report, Continental said it is nearing its long-term goal of raising net income to 2.5 percent of revenue.
